qualification: Retain exploratory metabolic function comparator: uncontrolled disease observations plus a small controlled sports signal, with no established BUBR1 restoration or MVA superiority.

studies.title: Effect of sodium pyruvate on exercise intolerance and muscle weakness due to mitochondrial myopathy: a case report
studies.evidence_class: Uncontrolled single-patient case report; hypothesis-generating clinical function observation

patient.diagnosis: Mitochondrial myopathy with mtDNA m.3271T>C, ragged-red fibers, some COX-deficient fibers and paracrystalline mitochondrial inclusions. This is not BUB1B-related MVA.
patient.context: Fatigue from age 15, worsening exercise intolerance at 18, proximal weakness and calf myalgia. Weight 40 kg, BMI 17.6. No muscle atrophy reported; Gowers sign positive.
patient.baseline_function: Neck flexion MMT 4; bilateral deltoid, iliopsoas, gluteus maximus and quadriceps MMT 4+. History of inability to climb school stairs and later walking difficulty due to myalgia; examination nevertheless reports no gait disturbance.
patient.metabolic_context: Serum lactate 54 mg/dL at admission, CK 1172 IU/L; blood gas analysis reported no abnormality. Describe hyperlactatemia, not demonstrated systemic acidemia.

preparation.route: Oral; aqueous solution specified in native Figure 3
preparation.timing: Figure 3 compares before treatment with after 2 weeks at 4 g/day; aqueous solution consumed between 11:00 and 13:00 on the illustrated day.
preparation.modification: Reduced to 3 g/day because of diarrhea; continued after discharge.
preparation.supplier: Acknowledgments credit Masashi Tanaka, Tokyo Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology, with supplying sodium pyruvate and treatment advice.
unknowns: Whether all subsequent concomitant doses remained identical

before_pyruvate: Dietary therapy: protein/fat/carbohydrate proportions 10–15%/50%/35–40%, reported fat 40–80 g/day
concomitants.important_boundary: CK normalized before sodium pyruvate while myalgia, fatigue, need for daily-activity assistance and hyperlactatemia persisted. Do not attribute that initial CK normalization to sodium pyruvate.

outcomes.name: Manual muscle strength
outcomes.result: Deltoid, iliopsoas, gluteus maximus and quadriceps strength reported to recover to MMT grade 5 from admission grade 4+ bilaterally.
outcomes.measurement_limit: Ordinal clinician assessment; no blinded assessment or quantitative dynamometry reported. Later neck-flexion grade not reported.

outcomes.name: Daily function and fatigue
outcomes.result: Further fatigue improvement; able to climb/descend stairs and go out.
outcomes.measurement_limit: Narrative function, no timed stairs, 6MWD, formal fatigue scale or controlled exercise capacity contrast.

outcomes.name: Pedometer steps
outcomes.time: Before versus after treatment in lactate comparison
outcomes.interpretation: Authors treated activity as similar; not evidence of increased walking capacity.

outcomes.name: Early-morning serum lactate
outcomes.interpretation: Uncontrolled biochemical change, not a treatment-effect estimate or BUBR1 assay.

outcomes.name: Diurnal lactate
outcomes.result: Native Figure 3 generally lower after therapy, but before/after curves converge around noon.
outcomes.measurement_limit: No sample replication, variance or inferential contrast; no universal suppression across every measurement.

outcomes.name: Muscle MRI
outcomes.result: Reduced abnormalities in gastrocnemius fat-saturated T2/STIR signal and gadolinium enhancement.
outcomes.measurement_limit: Native Figure 1 visually checked; descriptive imaging, not blinded quantitative muscle recovery.

harms_and_intercurrent_course.adverse_effect: Diarrhea attributed to treatment by authors; dose reduced from 4 to 3 g/day.
harms_and_intercurrent_course.month_7: After alcohol intake (350 mL drink, reported ethanol 11.2 g), headache/vomiting prevented food and medication intake; lactate 28.2 mg/dL and CK 677 IU/L. Rest, fluids and oral treatment restart accompanied improvement to lactate 19.2 and CK 91.
harms_and_intercurrent_course.causal_boundary: Not a controlled withdrawal/rechallenge: alcohol, vomiting, food intake, hydration, rest and medication interruption changed together. Do not attribute all deterioration to sodium pyruvate interruption.
harms_and_intercurrent_course.safety_limit: No systematic adverse-event denominator beyond one patient or comprehensive long-term safety assessment.

design.causality: Single before/after course amid other care cannot distinguish treatment from natural fluctuation, regression to the mean, co-treatment or observer effects.

studies.funding_and_interests: No grant funding statement identified in the five-page main; acknowledgments identify supplied pyruvate and clinical advice. Authors declare no relevant corporate/organizational COI.
studies.BUB1B_relevance: No BUB1B/BUBR1 level, spindle-checkpoint, chromosome-segregation or aneuploidy assay. Function observations remain clinically relevant as a metabolic-compensation hypothesis, not BUBR1 restoration or MVA efficacy.
studies.conclusion: Retain the actual positive function observations as hypothesis-grade clinical evidence; do not label the case a controlled efficacy demonstration.

studies.title: Effects of sodium pyruvate supplementation on repeated sprint exercise performance and recovery in male college soccer players: a randomized controlled trial
studies.evidence_class: Small randomized double-blind crossover, sport-specific direct function signal with statistical/reporting limitations

cohort.population: National-level male college soccer players; mean age 20 (SD 2), training 9 (SD 3) years, VO2max 55.93 (SD 5.36) mL/kg/min. Metabolic/cardiovascular disease excluded.

preparation.active: ≥99.0% sodium pyruvate from Lianlu Industrial Co., Ltd., Shanghai, China
preparation.form: Capsules similar in appearance, size, weight and reported taste; prepared as A/B by independent staff. Participants and test personnel blinded.
preparation.amount_and_duration: 0.1 g/kg/day for 7 days per condition; first 6 days quarter-dose four times daily, entire daily dose once on test day.
preparation.washout: 7-day washout between conditions; laboratory visits 14 days apart.
preparation.allocation: Counterbalanced randomized sequence; exact random sequence-generation and concealment procedures not detailed. Text states participants switched A/B.
preparation.reporting_discrepancy: Native Figure 1 repeats the same supplement labels in the second phase rather than depicting the A/B switch described in Methods.

studies.hierarchy: Main labels HIIE/RSE tests and blood collection under Primary outcome and estimated energy contributions under Secondary outcome. Attached three-page protocol describes these measures but supplies no dated prospective hierarchy or singled-out primary power comparison. Registry ChiCTR2100053936 cited; registry/history not independently retrieved.
studies.functional_protocol: Four 1-minute cycling intervals at 110% Wmax with 1-minute recovery; 10 minutes later six 6-second maximal cycling sprints with 24 seconds passive recovery. This is cycle performance in soccer athletes, not on-field play, chronic weakness or daily function.

positive_outcomes.endpoint: Mean relative peak power across six sprints
Mean relative mean power across six sprints

nulls: No significant treatment advantage marked for peak-power sprints 2, 3, 4 or 6, or mean-power sprints 1, 2, 3, 4 or 6 in Figure 2.
Estimated total aerobic contribution during HIIE p=.275 and total glycolytic contribution p=.411.
Discussion reports blood lactate concentrations did not differ.
Post-RSE pH and bicarbonate not marked as different versus placebo in Table 2, although base excess was.
studies.mechanistic_context: Higher pH/bicarbonate/base excess at selected times; higher estimated phosphagen regeneration (total HIIE p=.029, RSE p=.041). ATP-PCr was estimated from oxygen uptake, not measured in muscle, and is not demonstrated mediation.
statistical_limits: Averaged power and energy outcomes used independent-samples t tests despite repeated exposure of the same participants; attached protocol repeats this. The analysis does not use within-person pairing for these averages, and no valid paired effect CI can be recovered here.
Multiple sprint/time/outcome comparisons with Fisher LSD; no family-wide multiplicity correction reported.

No period, sequence or carryover analysis of power outcomes reported. The reported nonsignificant supplementation-order check for baseline blood pH, bicarbonate and base excess does not establish absence of power-outcome carryover.
Sample-size calculation targeted acid-base balance, not the selected power endpoints.
No raw paired dataset; numerical power outcomes primarily graphical, and no outcome CI printed.
studies.harms: No participant reported gastrointestinal discomfort with either capsule. Short exposure and small n do not establish broader safety; one dropout before randomization attributed to personal reasons.
studies.funding_and_interests: National Key R&D Program of China 2018YFC2000600 and Herbalife Winter Sports Development Fund KBL2019003. FQ Zhou affiliated with Shanghai Sandai Pharmaceutical R&D Co. Ltd.; other authors declare no conflicts.
studies.conclusion: Preserve controlled power positives with the exact active preparation and placebo. Limit to a small athlete cycling context; not clinical mitochondrial-myopathy/MVA efficacy or BUB1B rescue.

reported_order_check.source_location: Results, Blood gas analysis, immediately before Table 2 discussion
reported_order_check.outcomes: Baseline blood pH, HCO3− and base excess
reported_order_check.result: No significant supplementation-order effect reported for these baseline blood measures (all P>0.05).
reported_order_check.limit: This is not a reported order/period/carryover analysis of power outcomes, and nonsignificance does not prove absence of carryover.

article.title: Efficacy of pyruvate therapy in patients with mitochondrial disease: A semi-quantitative clinical evaluation study

design.type: Uncontrolled longitudinal four-patient clinical series with open withdrawal/rechallenge observations in two patients; not a randomized or concurrent-controlled trial.
design.selection: Patients already receiving pyruvate for more than 12 months; total treated/eligible population and early discontinuers not enumerated.
design.registration_and_hierarchy: No registry identifier or prospectively fixed primary endpoint/response threshold reported in the main. No external historical registry audit.
design.concomitants: Other mitochondrial disease medications maintained unchanged during monitoring; full patient-by-patient inventory not supplied. Coenzyme Q10 before pyruvate noted for patient 3.
design.consent: Institutional ethics approval and written parental consent reported.

preparation.identity: Sodium pyruvate from Musashino Chemical Laboratory, Tokyo
preparation.study_exposure: 0.5 g/kg/day in two divided doses; increased to 1.0 g/kg/day in patient 3
preparation.vehicle: Water, approximately 2–10%; concentration adjusted for hydration/volume tolerance
preparation.full_composition: Purity, excipients and full product/batch specifications not supplied. Do not transfer to calcium pyruvate, mixtures, or arbitrary commercial products.
preparation.scope: Research exposure description, not clinical regimen advice.

endpoints.NPMDS: Sections I–III objective clinical/functional/system assessments; section IV parent-reported quality of life. Higher score is worse. Different age versions used in patients 3 and 4.
endpoints.GMFM88: Higher is better. Only lying/rolling (A) and sitting (B) assessable; C–E treated as zero, total mean across five dimensions. Not validated specifically for mitochondrial disease.
endpoints.endpoint_patient_n: NPMDS reported for all four at some evaluation; GMFM for patients 1–3, absent for patient 4. Patient 2 initially assessed by JMDRS, later NPMDS/GMFM after washout. Late NPMDS not done for patient 1.
endpoints.statistics: Mann–Whitney U tests only for serial biochemical data; no controlled functional effect estimates, functional P values, CIs, or reported multiplicity adjustment.

patient_results.observed_function: Gained rolling and supine leg elevation from no more than 45 degrees to 90 degrees; more active arm movements. Maintained at late evaluation.
patient_results.withdrawal_rechallenge: After initial response, open withdrawal produced lethargy within 1–2 weeks and status epilepticus after 19 days; resumption restored pre-withdrawal clinical state. Not randomized or blinded.

patient_results.initial_history: Could roll and fully feed orally at 12 months; authors considered natural development a possible explanation. Viral-associated encephalopathy at age 3 led to loss of these abilities.
patient_results.washout_rechallenge: Four-week withdrawal at age 5 years 3 months did not cause deterioration; resumption produced no two-month scale improvement.
patient_results.qualification: No persuasive treatment-associated functional response reported.

patient_results.disease: Nonspecific encephalomyopathy, combined complex I and IV deficiency; no mtDNA mutation identified, nuclear analysis ongoing
patient_results.observed_function: Initially gained bilateral rolling and lost dysphagia; later motor regression and poorer head control. Global NPMDS nevertheless improved with seizure/GI/hepatic changes.
patient_results.harm: Mild chronic diarrhea throughout therapy, considered a treatment side effect.
patient_results.qualification: Early motor signal regressed; do not equate improving overall disease score with sustained motor improvement.

patient_results.disease: Myopathic mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome progressing to encephalomyopathy; tracheostomy and respirator
patient_results.observed_function: Forearm elevation improved from absent to 90 degrees at two months; numerical early NPMDS improvement entirely in subjective section IV. Status epilepticus and new brain lesions followed at three months; severe later decline.
patient_results.overlap: Explicitly the previously published Saito et al. 2012 case (BBA 1820:632–636; reference 3). Not an independent replication.

aggregate_interpretation.counterevidence: Two initially responsive patients later lost motor improvement; patient 2 lacked persuasive response. Patient 3 overall NPMDS improved despite motor regression.
aggregate_interpretation.blood_markers: Lactate, lactate/pyruvate and amino-acid changes were not significant and did not track clinical response. Serial samples are repeated measurements within four patients, not additional independent patients.
aggregate_interpretation.causal_limit: Small selected heterogeneous uncontrolled series, unblinded assessment, natural history/development, concomitants and different scale versions limit causal attribution. Withdrawal/rechallenge in patient 1 strengthens temporal association but is not a controlled group effect.
aggregate_interpretation.harms: One mild chronic diarrhea case at 1 g/kg/day. Seizure/status episodes and disease progression also described; temporal descriptions do not prove drug causality. Four cases cannot establish general safety.

overlap.Saito2012: CONFIRMED: patient 4 is the same case; do not count as independent replication.
overlap.Kuroha2015: Profiles support distinct cases: retained Kuroha main describes a 19-year-old woman, onset fatigue age 15 and m.3271T>C; Fujii cases have onset/presentation in childhood and different disease/genotype descriptions. This assessment uses actual clinical profiles, not merely publication dates; no participant-ID linkage performed.
overlap.other_or_later_cohorts: Not established; do not assume independence from other pyruvate series, including later reports.

studies.funding: Japanese MEXT research grants and Global COE; Takeda Science Foundation; MHLW intractable-disease grants H23-016, H23-119, H24-005; Kawano Masanori Memorial pediatric foundation.
studies.conflicts: Authors declare no conflicts of interest.

notice_check.pubmed: No linked CommentsCorrectionsList in retrieved record.
notice_check.crossref: No update-to/updated-by or relation notice in retained record.
notice_check.limit: Bounded metadata check, not complete publisher Crossmark history.

studies.decision: Retain a small, preparation-specific clinical motor signal, strongest in patient 1, with explicit uncontrolled and non-independent-case limits. No BUB1B/BUBR1 endpoint, no MVA efficacy, no comparative superiority or regimen recommendation.
studies.source_reading_depth: Complete six-page main and native Tables 1–3 from official institutional scans; independent complete relevant-source check.

source.title: Biomarkers and clinical rating scales for sodium pyruvate therapy in patients with mitochondrial disease
source.version_read: Native publisher article page 11 deposited in coauthor Kazan repository; complete PubMed abstract; publisher bibliographic API/Crossref metadata. The deposited PDF is only one page.

design.reported: 48-week prospective single-centre exploratory clinical study; biomarkers and scales measured at baseline, 12 and 48 weeks.
design.randomization: Not reported in accessible primary text.
design.control: No comparator or between-group effect reported in accessible text; reported results compare follow-up with baseline. Do not award controlled-efficacy credit.
design.prespecified_hierarchy: Unknown: no linked/verified trial registry or protocol obtained. The abstract describes exploration of biomarkers/scales to inform a future trial, not a verified prospective primary-endpoint hierarchy.
design.analysis_method: Not available; statistical tests, multiplicity handling and missing-data method unverified.

preparation.interpretation_limit: Retain this printed notation without converting it to a verified total daily amount or clinical regimen; dosing schedule and main-method confirmation unavailable.
preparation.gap: Actual administered preparation, concomitant medicines/diet and adherence cannot be verified from the available page. A manufacturer page citing the paper is not proof that its listed reagent was used.

cohort.population: Japanese adults with genetically, biochemically and clinically confirmed mitochondrial disease and intractable lactic acidosis, as described by authors.
cohort.death_context: Two patients already had end-stage MELAS at baseline and died during sodium pyruvate therapy.
cohort.death_attribution: Not established by the accessible abstract or first page. Do not infer treatment causation or dismissal as unrelated.
cohort.denominator_boundary: Eleven is enrollment, not verified analysis or 48-week completion n. Eleven minus two deaths is not evidence that nine supplied any endpoint.
cohort.missingness: Timing of deaths, other loss, endpoint exclusions, complete-case versus imputed analysis and survivor selection cannot be assessed.

clinical_scales.name: JMDRS
clinical_scales.comparison: Reported follow-up versus baseline; no controlled contrast

clinical_scales.name: NMDAS overall
clinical_scales.comparison: Reported follow-up versus baseline; no controlled contrast
clinical_scales.reported_result: No significant decrease; authors describe a tendency
clinical_scales.boundary: P=.059 does not establish efficacy. No exact magnitude, clinically important difference, subdomain benefit or useful-function improvement can be verified.

studies.other_endpoints: FGF21 and pyruvate were measured, but the accessible abstract does not establish their exact results; omission from positive summary is not proof of a null. Week-12 results and individual functional trajectories not verified.
studies.function_interpretation: Retain reported biochemical positives; they do not substitute for a clinical scale improvement, direct strength/walking benefit, controlled effect, or mediation. A nonsignificant overall scale result is not proof of no benefit in every patient.
studies.harms: Two deaths are reported, but no full adverse-event table, other event counts, GI effects, withdrawals, dose reductions or safety ascertainment procedures are accessible. Safety cannot be established.

cohort_overlap.reason: Native introduction cites earlier small pyruvate reports, but patient identities, genotypes and cross-report mappings are not available on page 11. Shared authors or citations are not proof of overlap or independence.
cohort_overlap.boundary: Do not count as independent replication of Kuroha 2015, Fujii 2014 or earlier case reports without linkage.

publisher_deposited_crossref_funders: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology
Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development
funding_and_interests.crossref_award: JP17ek0109088h00 (as deposited; full acknowledgments not read)
funding_and_interests.boundary: Metadata is not a substitute for the unavailable main disclosures.

studies.BUB1B_MVA: No direct BUB1B/BUBR1 restoration evidence in accessible text. No MVA cohort or MVA functional efficacy established. Full-paper assay coverage cannot be certified from one page.

notice_check.interpretation: No linked notice identified in these retained metadata records; publisher Crossmark history not independently audited.

studies.decision: Keep as an incomplete primary clinical context source: biochemical positives with nonsignificant clinical-scale results, deaths and major denominator/method gaps. Do not upgrade to controlled clinical-function evidence or assert a definitive negative efficacy conclusion.
studies.scope: External clinical2019 folder only; frozen primary/independent sources and repository unchanged; no clinical regimen recommendation.
studies.source_reading_depth: Complete abstract and native first page only. Full main, endpoint denominators, exact scale changes, statistical methods and detailed harms unavailable.

physiology_context.depth: PubMed abstract plus targeted full-text subjects, protocol and results text; native figures not inspected and not fully appraised.
physiology_context.classification: Randomized double-blind crossover physiological study in nine active men, not a demonstrated maximal-performance effect.
physiology_context.finding: Fixed 2-minute 50 W then 6-minute ~90% VO2max task after single sodium pyruvate or placebo. Acid-base change and higher post-exercise lactate; overall gas-exchange response not improved. Do not classify merely performing the fixed task as a functional efficacy endpoint.

BUB1B_BUBR1.result: No direct pyruvate intervention restoring BUB1B/BUBR1 identified in this bounded search; not a universal absence claim.

verified_primary_context.title: The progeroid gene BubR1 regulates axon myelination and motor function
verified_primary_context.depth: Relevant oligodendrocyte-culture Methods paragraph read; full scientific article not appraised.
verified_primary_context.finding: 1 mM sodium pyruvate is a constituent of routine glial-cell culture medium. BubR1 expression staining does not turn the shared medium into a pyruvate treatment comparison.

BUB1B_BUBR1.other_search_hits: Additional hits concerned culture media, genetic rescue or pyruvate kinase rather than pyruvate administration; not promoted to intervention evidence.

cohort_deduplication: Fujii patient 4 is the previously published Saito 2012 case; Kuroha adult profile is distinct. Later-series overlap remains unresolved; do not sum report denominators into a unique-patient total.
competitiveness: No direct or indirect evidence here establishes superiority to the provisional nominees. Useful function, exposure, renewal and chromosome fidelity are reciprocal requirements; functional BUBR1 mediation is additionally needed only for a restoration claim. Redox plausibility does not transfer NMN/SIRT2/BUBR1 results to sodium pyruvate.
scope: Study preparations and observations, not clinical regimens or current retail-product equivalence. No new original-queue reading or biological-replication credit. Broader discovery remains incomplete.

root_reading.kuroha2015: All five native rendered pages visually inspected, including Japanese clinical course and English abstract. Interpreted as a source appraisal, not certified translation or independent medical-image diagnosis.
root_reading.yang2022: Selected original Methods/statistics/Results/blood-order text and native Figure2 all panels; source and independent qualifications read. Not a complete root re-read of the entire main/protocol.
root_reading.independent_review: findings.md read; PASS with resolved power-versus-blood order-analysis distinction.
